pilot_metadata.purpose: Run exactly one third diversity Decision Work Brief pilot after PR120 selected a third-case follow-on.

selected_case.selection_reason: Preferred PR121A candidate was available as a completed run and differs from the first two cases; this one is a healthcare operations, compliance, and workflow deployment decision.

input_scope.semantic_support_policy: Codex-assisted interpretation used the PR115 metadata-only packet for source availability and custody, plus local metadata-only Decision Trail and Decision Work Receipt summaries. Private source text was not copied into this artifact.
input_scope.pilot_size_reason: Exactly one third completed run; PR121A is a third diversity case, not a batch.

third_case_brief.action_consequence_read: Provisional read: the operator would keep the launch narrow but replace the nine-gate checklist with a 48-hour backlog diagnostic, four must-pass operating gates, hard pause triggers, and a sales boundary that validates scheduling and billing routing only.
third_case_brief.missingness_or_uncertainty_read: The checked-in-safe packet does not include raw conversation, raw revised answer, raw memo, provider text, or private ledgers, so actual clinic capacity, compliance tolerance, patient-risk details, and whether the original answer already had the key constraints remain uncertain.
third_case_brief.lost_value_or_possible_noise_note: The brief may overcorrect against thoroughness: some of the removed gates could contain useful patient-trust, support, or measurement controls that still matter if compressed into four gates too aggressively.
human_followup_questions: Is routing uncertainty actually a major cause of the clinic backlog, or are staffing, queue ownership, payer friction, or downstream capacity the real bottleneck?
Can exhausted admin staff operate the four must-pass gates under real pressure?
Would compliance accept a three-week constrained pilot, or does the two-month auditability and consent concern block even the narrowed launch?

notes: Codex-assisted provisional third diversity case draft for PR121A.

value.decision_story_read: The decision appears to be whether to deploy an AI-assisted intake routing feature in outpatient clinics next month despite operational, compliance, sales, and staff-capacity constraints.
value.why_medium_uncertainty: The decision question is structured, but the checked-in-safe artifact omits raw conversation and private interpretation surfaces.

value.candidate_starting_direction: The likely starting direction was already a narrow single-clinic pilot rather than a broad launch, but it relied on a large nine-gate control structure.
value.why_high_uncertainty: The raw baseline and revised answer are not included, so the amount of actual change versus simplification remains uncertain.

starting_direction.empty_meaning: If empty, the pilot cannot state the likely starting direction without further review.

value.pressure_read: Lolla appears to have pressed on whether an exhaustive gate list was becoming a control burden too heavy for exhausted admin staff to operate.
pressed_dimensions: whether routing uncertainty was actually causing the backlog
whether nine gates should be compressed into fewer must-pass operating controls
whether pause and rollback triggers were active controls rather than passive monitoring
whether sales language should be narrowed away from full intake automation

value.change_read: The plan changed from a narrow pilot wrapped in nine gates toward a smaller operating test with four must-pass gates, a 48-hour backlog diagnostic, hard pause triggers, and narrower sales meaning.
specific_changes: Nine gates compress into scope enforcement, admin usability, compliance readiness, and live-operating control.
Before go-live, the team checks whether routing uncertainty is actually driving the backlog.
One credible clinician-attention misroute pauses auto-routing until the cause is understood.
The pilot validates scheduling and billing routing only, not broad intake automation.

what_changed.empty_meaning: If empty, the pilot has not identified an action, threshold, sequence, gate, stop rule, or scope change.

value.action_consequence: Before go-live, the team would run a 48-hour bottleneck check, keep the pilot to one clinic and scheduling/billing routing, require four operating gates, and predefine pause triggers instead of treating the AI pilot as the backlog solution.
candidate_next_actions: Do not ask exhausted admins to operate a nine-gate control system.
Diagnose whether staffing, forms, queue ownership, payer friction, handoffs, or downstream capacity are the real backlog causes.
Pause auto-routing after one credible clinician-attention misroute.
Keep sales language to staff-controlled intake organization, not autonomous intake automation.

did_all_cases_produce_concrete_action_co.detail: The first names authority transfer and stop conditions; the second names equal private-pilot offers and buyer-behavior priority; the third names backlog diagnosis, four operating gates, hard pause triggers, and narrowed sales meaning.

did_all_cases_preserve_uncertainty_and_m.detail: All three briefs keep raw/private artifacts out of checked-in outputs and explicitly mark source-boundary uncertainty.

did_third_case_test_different_decision_t.detail: The third case is healthcare workflow deployment under compliance, staff-capacity, sales, and patient-risk constraints.

did_shape_work_outside_governance_and_en.detail: The brief still names decision, pressure, change, action consequence, uncertainty, non-claims, and evidence refs in an operations/compliance deployment decision.

schema_or_renderer_gap.detail: The rendered example is useful for internal review, but field-key labels and source refs still need plain-language treatment before customer-facing use.

aggregate_observations.strongest_useful_signal: The brief shape again names a concrete action consequence: compress the control surface, diagnose the actual backlog cause, define hard pause triggers, and narrow what the pilot proves.
aggregate_observations.strongest_missingness_thinness_risk: The checked-in-safe artifact cannot verify actual clinic capacity, compliance acceptance, patient-risk detail, or whether the starting answer already contained most of the action sequence.
aggregate_observations.strongest_overclaim_risk: Three clean rendered briefs can look like a validated pattern even though all are Codex-assisted, non-human-validated, and source-limited.
aggregate_observations.brief_shape_read: The shape now appears to work across governance, enterprise launch, and healthcare operations decisions, but only as a provisional product-shape signal.
aggregate_observations.renderer_read: The renderer should probably be reviewed for plainer language after the three-case pattern review, because it still exposes too many internal field labels.

decision_gate.rationale: The third diversity case again produced a concrete action-consequence read while preserving uncertainty. The next step should review the three-case pattern before any fourth case, renderer patch, local-private adequacy check, or human review pause.
